_comment: Scenario presets to GENERATE from the vanilla 1836 start (tools/extract_presets.ps1 -> ui/presets.js). Each entry is one country's WHOLE MARKET: the lead country plus every subject that shares its market (all subject types share the overlord's market unless a `grant_own_market` pact exists — read live from common/history/diplomacy/00_subject_relationships.txt). 'market_add' / 'market_drop' are manual overrides on that member list (tags, no c: prefix). 'sol' is the per-class wealth level whose buy package the class consumes (defaults below) — except 'slaves', which is not a standard of living the pops spend against but the SLAVE BASKET level the employing buildings buy: derived from the lower stratum by the game's own SLAVE_BASKET_* clamp, then overwritten by the measured slave SoL where there is one (that measurement IS the realised basket). The UI always offers a built-in 'Empty' preset on top of these.

defaults._class_mult_comment: Optional overrides for how much of its buy package a class brings to the market. Omitted classes use the game's own numbers where they exist: peasants = consumption_mult from common/pop_types/peasants.txt (0.05). There is deliberately NO 'slaves' entry — slaves buy nothing, so they are not on this path at all; the building that employs them buys them a basket, and that basket takes no class multiplier.

presets._comment: PLACEHOLDER scenarios - synthetic, NOT derived from any country. One level of every ordinary building so that every production chain is present exactly once, which is what BE-solving wants. Deliberately uniform and deliberately crude: diversify them later. A `placeholder` block replaces `country`/`measured_market` entirely. lower_sol is ALWAYS the LOWER stratum's standard of living and drives everything: middle = 1.5x, upper = 3x (per the user's rule), the slave basket comes from the game's SLAVE_BASKET_* clamp on lower_sol, and the base wage comes from FINDINGS F26, base = exp((SoL-37.43)/10.49).
presets.label: Placeholder SoL 8

placeholder_defaults._comment: Shared by every `placeholder` preset. Pops are flat counts; within-stratum variation is the UI's own SOL_SPREAD, not something the preset carries. peasant_sol_offset is added to lower_sol - measured 1836 puts peasants within ~0.5 of the lower stratum either way (Belgium +0.5, Austria -0.4), so 0 is the honest default rather than a guess.
placeholder_defaults._exclude_comment: Company headquarters are excluded as SPECIAL: they exist only once a company is formed, so they are not part of any ordinary chain. Manor houses and financial districts are kept - they are ordinary ownership buildings, they employ the upper stratum this scenario has, and they carry no market goods either way.
